items.title: 美財長貝森特籲Fed保持「開放態度」：AI生產率紅利或緩解通膨壓力
items.title_en: Treasury Secretary Borenstein Urges Fed to Keep an "Open Mind": AI Productivity Gains Could Ease Inflation Pressure
paras: 美國財長貝森特最新呼籲，Fed在評估通膨與利率路徑時應保持「開放態度」，他並認為AI帶來的生產率提升以及監管放鬆，有望擴大美國經濟的供給能力，進而從根本上抑制價格壓力。
貝森特此番發言正值Fed本月重啟升息、市場重估緊縮幅度之際，凸顯財政部與貨幣政策當局在通膨判斷上的微妙分歧。
貝森特援引Fed前主席葛林斯潘的歷史經驗指出，在生產率快速提升的環境下，經濟具備更大的擴張空間。他認為，當前美國經濟正受益於減稅、監管放鬆及技術進步，決策官員不應忽視這些供給端的正面變化。
在通膨構成上，貝森特試圖區分「能源衝擊」與「基礎通膨」。他指出，儘管中東局勢推高汽油價格，加大消費者生活成本，但剔除能源與食品後的核心CPI表現相對溫和。
美國8月核心CPI年增2.4%，雖仍高於2%的目標，但近期實際已有所回落。貝森特認為，能源價格衝擊並不一定會轉化為廣泛的基礎通膨壓力。
然而，Fed立場更為謹慎。面對通膨風險，Fed本月中升息1碼至3.75%-4%，多位官員強調需保持政策的限制性。
貝森特則將當前AI發展類比於1990年代的網路革命，認為更快的生產率增長能允許經濟以更高速度運行，同時減輕工資上漲轉化為通脹的壓力。
這場關於「通膨來源」的辯論，亦即外部供給衝擊還是內部需求過熱所致，將決定Fed未來利率路徑，而貝森特最新表態則顯示，在Fed重啟升息後，財政部對進一步緊縮持保留態度，並希望為潛在增長率的提升保留政策空間。
paras_en: U.S. Treasury Secretary Borenstein recently called on the Fed to maintain an "open mind" when assessing inflation and the interest‑rate path, arguing that productivity gains from AI and regulatory easing could expand the United States’ supply capacity and fundamentally curb price pressures.

Borenstein’s remarks come as the Fed resumes rate hikes this month and markets reassess the degree of monetary tightening, highlighting a subtle divergence between the Treasury and the central bank on how to judge inflation.

Citing former Fed Chair Alan Greenspan’s historical experience, Borenstein noted that an environment of rapid productivity growth gives the economy more room to expand. He said the U.S. economy is currently benefiting from tax cuts, deregulation and technological progress, and policymakers should not overlook these positive supply‑side developments.

On the composition of inflation, Borenstein tried to separate an "energy shock" from "core inflation." He pointed out that although Middle‑East tensions have pushed gasoline prices higher and increased consumer living costs, core CPI—excluding energy and food—has been relatively moderate.

U.S. core CPI rose 2.4% year‑over‑year in August, still above the 2% target but showing a recent decline. Borenstein said the energy price shock does not necessarily translate into broad‑based core inflation pressure.

The Fed, however, remains more cautious. Facing inflation risks, the central bank raised rates by a quarter point this month to a target range of 3.75%‑4%, and several officials emphasized the need to keep policy restrictive.

Borenstein likened the current AI boom to the internet revolution of the 1990s, arguing that faster productivity growth can allow the economy to run at a higher speed while easing the pressure of wage growth feeding into inflation.

The debate over the source of inflation—whether it stems from external supply shocks or overheated domestic demand—will shape the Fed’s future rate path. Borenstein’s latest stance shows that after the Fed’s rate‑hike restart, the Treasury remains hesitant about further tightening and wants to preserve policy space to boost the potential growth rate.

items.title: 比爾蓋茲警告AI恐致10億人死亡！反駁川普：政府監管不會削弱美中競爭
items.title_en: Bill Gates Warns AI Could Cause One Billion Deaths, Counters Trump: Government Regulation Won't Undermine US-China Competition
paras: 微軟(MSFT-US) 共同創辦人比爾蓋茲（Bill Gates）警告，人工智慧（AI）已是「強大到足以」殺死大部分人類的工具，他也加入越來越多科技業領袖與員工的行列，呼籲外界正視AI可能對人類生存造成的風險，與美國總統川普大致不願積極介入的立場形成對比，並認為這不會讓美國落後於中國。
根據《彭博》報導，蓋茲在接受《NBC》訪問時表示，「AI確實強大到足以引發一些事件，導致10億人死亡。」
他表示：「從未有任何武器，能像懷有惡意的人使用最新AI工具這種組合一樣強大。」
蓋茲的立場也與川普相反。他認為，美國政府針對人工智慧（AI）潛在災難性風險建立安全防護措施，不會削弱美國與中國競爭的能力。
他說：「當然，所有國家都應該希望建立這些安全防護措施。所以對於那些聲稱『中國不會建立這些安全防護措施』的說法，我完全不同意。」
面對低迷的民調支持度，以及共和黨在11月選舉中力拚維持國會控制權，川普將AI可能威脅人類生存的警告形容為一場騙局，認為這種說法可能阻礙美國創新，並讓中國從中得利。
當被問及川普的相關言論時，蓋茲則表示：「這完全不是騙局。」
他預期，中國也會支持AI安全措施，因為中國同樣不希望成為攻擊目標。蓋茲並認為，川普在「聽取我以及其他人的意見後」，可能改變立場，其中包括讓川普了解，AI安全措施並不會削弱美國在他所認為的「國家間競爭」中的能力。
隨著AI模型能力快速提升，矽谷近期對AI可能造成災難性後果的警告也持續增加。
Anthropic員工Jacob Coxon本月稍早離職，並公開批評Anthropic與OpenAI持續競逐超級智慧AI，形容相關企業是在拿人類生命「下注」，因為兩家公司正「競相開發超級智慧AI」。
另一名Anthropic員工則表示，他認為AI在未來10年消滅全人類的機率超過10%。
這些言論讓原本長期存在於AI產業內部、且具爭議性的AI生存風險討論，進一步受到大眾關注，也引發外界要求AI業者強化安全措施。
Anthropic執行長阿莫戴（Dario Amodei）此後呼籲放緩AI開發速度，OpenAI執行長奧特曼（Sam Altman）及馬斯克等人也表達支持。
蓋茲認為，面對AI可能帶來的風險，業界自律並不足夠，政府及執法機構必須參與制定安全防護與監控機制，並將相關要求納入強制規範。
蓋茲此前也曾在8月發表文章指出，隨著AI工具能力持續提升，惡意人士可能利用AI發動網路攻擊、詐欺及散播錯誤資訊，並對醫院、金融機構、電網及政府系統等造成大規模傷害。
對於「kill switch」（緊急關停開關）概念，也就是確保人類在強大AI模型開始出現危險行為時，仍有能力停止或限制模型運作，蓋茲則指出，這項措施「還不夠」，也無法取代更早階段的監督機制。
他表示：「我們確實需要監控任何複雜的模型，並完整記錄究竟進行了哪些操作。美國應該確保這些措施落實，中國也會希望這麼做。」
（本文不開放合作夥伴轉載）
paras_en: Microsoft (MSFT-US) co‑founder Bill Gates warned that artificial intelligence (AI) is already "powerful enough" to become a tool that could kill most of humanity. He joined a growing number of tech leaders and employees urging the world to take the existential risks of AI seriously, contrasting with President Donald Trump’s generally reluctant stance on active involvement, and he believes this will not let the United States fall behind China.
According to Bloomberg, Gates told NBC that "AI is indeed powerful enough to trigger events that could lead to one billion deaths."
He said, "No weapon has ever been as powerful as the combination of malicious people using the latest AI tools."
Gates’s position also runs opposite to Trump’s. He believes that U.S. government safety measures against AI’s potentially catastrophic risks will not weaken America’s ability to compete with China.
He added, "Of course every country should want to build these safety safeguards. So I completely disagree with the claim that ‘China won’t build these safeguards.’"

Facing low poll support and a Republican push to retain congressional control in the November election, Trump dismissed the warning that AI could threaten human survival as a hoax, arguing that such claims could stifle U.S. innovation and benefit China.
When asked about Trump’s remarks, Gates responded, "It is absolutely not a hoax."

He expects China will also back AI safety measures because it likewise does not want to become a target of attacks. Gates believes that after "listening to me and others," Trump might change his stance, including understanding that AI safety does not diminish U.S. capability in what he calls "inter‑national competition."
As AI model capabilities surge, warnings from Silicon Valley about possible disastrous outcomes have been mounting recently.

Anthropic employee Jacob Coxon left the company earlier this month and publicly criticized Anthropic and OpenAI for racing toward super‑intelligent AI, describing the firms as "betting on human lives" as they "compete to develop super‑intelligent AI."
Another Anthropic employee said he believes the probability that AI will wipe out all humanity within the next ten years exceeds 10%.

These statements have brought the long‑standing, controversial internal AI‑industry debate over existential risk into the public eye, prompting calls for stronger safety measures from outside the sector.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei subsequently urged a slowdown in AI development, and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman as well as Elon Musk also voiced support for the call.

Gates argues that industry self‑regulation is insufficient to address AI risks; governments and law‑enforcement agencies must take part in creating safety safeguards and monitoring mechanisms, and embed those requirements into binding regulations.

Gates previously wrote in August that as AI tools become more capable, malicious actors could use AI to launch cyber attacks, fraud and disinformation, causing large‑scale harm to hospitals, financial institutions, power grids and government systems.

Regarding the "kill switch" concept—ensuring humanity can shut down or limit a powerful AI model when it begins to behave dangerously—Gates said the measure is "still not enough" and cannot replace earlier‑stage oversight mechanisms.

He said, "We do need to monitor any complex model and fully log what operations are being performed. The United States should ensure these measures are implemented, and China would also want to do the same."
(This article is not open for partner re‑publication)

items.title: 〈VSMC開幕〉VSMC一期全滿 方略：二期規劃加速 不排除導入28/22奈米
items.title_en: VSMC Opening: Phase‑1 Fully Booked, Strategy Accelerates Phase‑2 Planning, May Adopt 28/22‑nm Process
paras: 世界先進(5347-TW)暨VSMC董事長方略今(28)日表示，目前VSMC進度優於預期，今年第四季就有機會進入風險性試產，維持明年第一季量產計畫，包括電源以及矽中介層(Interposer)等產品都會開始產出，包括損益兩平、獲利、滿載的時間點都有機會提前，甚至已經接獲不少客戶需求，正在評估各項條件，坦言二期規劃正在加速中，也不排除更進一步往22/28奈米製程前進。
VSMC一期採用130奈米至40奈米製程，生產混合訊號、電源管理、類比產品及矽中介層等產品，預期2029年產能達滿載，每月產能為12吋44,000片晶圓，可望創造約1,600個工作機會。
方略指出，一期產能已全數被客戶預訂，後續新增需求只能等待二期開出，因此公司已開始蒐集財務、客戶需求及技術定位等相關條件，暗示會在「短暫的將來」評估二期的啟動時程。對於外界關注二期是否可能在今年底定案、明年動工，方略則表示，公司沒有那麼著急，仍會「謀定而後動」，但一旦決定啟動，就會快速執行。
VSMC目前已開始初步蒐集二期所需評估的各項條件，包括財務狀況、客戶需求、技術定位與應用方向。方略強調，12吋晶圓廠投資金額龐大，如果定位錯誤，未來可能形成結構性問題，因此一定要把財務、需求與技術方向都想清楚後才會正式啟動。
方略認為，相較第一期，未來二期若正式啟動，整體難度將相對降低。隨著第一座12吋廠跨過建廠與量產門檻，世界先進營收將大幅成長，未來進行第二座廠投資時，財務壓力可望下降。此外，經歷一期建廠後，團隊的建廠經驗與執行能力都已大幅提升，且部分廠務設施與建築基礎已經完成，因此理論上二期的啟動難度也會低於一期。
針對二期是否可能引進第三個合作夥伴，方略則明確表示，目前沒有這項規劃，二期仍會與恩智浦(NXPI-US)共同合作，不會再尋找第三方加入。
量產進度方面，方略表示，今年第四季已有機會進行部分風險性試產，但正式計畫仍維持明年第一季進入量產的目標，目前看來第一季量產的把握度相當高，產品將涵蓋電源管理及矽中介層(Interposer)等相關產品。
至於原先規劃2029年達到滿載，方略表示，以目前進度來看，「應該要達成是沒有什麼問題的目標」，甚至有機會提前實現。
對於二期投資金額與技術內容，方略仍保持審慎。他指出，真正決定投資規模的關鍵，在於未來要做什麼產品、採用什麼技術與鎖定何種應用，目前這些定位尚未完全確定，因此仍不宜過早給出具體數字。
方略強調，一旦二期的技術與產品方向確定，公司就能進一步說明投資金額、產能與時程；現階段最重要的仍是持續聽取客戶需求，確保新的12吋投資能建立在清楚且可長期發展的市場定位之上。
paras_en: World Advanced (5347‑TW) and VSMC Chairman Fang Lue said today (the 28th) that VSMC’s progress is ahead of schedule and that a risky pilot run could begin in Q4 this year, keeping the plan for mass production in Q1 next year. Power‑management chips and silicon interposer products will start shipping, and break‑even, profitability and full‑load milestones could all be moved forward. The company has already received numerous customer requests and is evaluating the conditions, noting that Phase‑2 planning is being accelerated and that moving to a 22/28‑nm process is not ruled out.

Phase‑1 uses 130‑nm to 40‑nm processes to produce mixed‑signal, power‑management, analog and silicon‑interposer products. Full capacity is expected by 2029, with a monthly output of 44,000 12‑inch wafers, which could create about 1,600 jobs.

Fang noted that Phase‑1 capacity is already fully booked, and any additional demand will have to wait for Phase‑2. The company has begun gathering financial, customer‑demand and technology‑positioning data, hinting that it will assess the Phase‑2 start‑up timing in the "near future." Regarding speculation that Phase‑2 could be finalized by year‑end and break ground next year, he said the company is not in a hurry, will plan carefully before acting, but will move quickly once a decision is made.

VSMC has started to collect the various conditions needed to evaluate Phase‑2, including financial status, customer demand, technology positioning and application direction. Fang stressed that a 12‑inch fab requires massive investment, and a wrong positioning could create structural problems, so all financial, demand and technical aspects must be clarified before formally launching Phase‑2.

Fang believes that, compared with Phase‑1, the overall difficulty of a formally launched Phase‑2 will be lower. With the first 12‑inch fab crossing construction and mass‑production thresholds, World Advanced’s revenue will grow sharply, reducing financial pressure for a second fab. Moreover, after building Phase‑1, the team’s construction experience and execution capability have improved markedly, and some facilities and building foundations are already in place, so theoretically Phase‑2 should be easier to start than Phase‑1.

Regarding whether a third partner might join Phase‑2, Fang stated clearly that there is no such plan; Phase‑2 will continue to be a joint effort with NXP (NXPI‑US) and no additional partner will be sought.

On mass‑production timing, Fang said there is an opportunity for limited risky pilot runs in Q4 this year, but the official schedule still targets mass production in Q1 next year. The outlook for a Q1 start is strong, and the product lineup will include power‑management chips and silicon interposers among others.
As for the original plan to reach full capacity by 2029, Fang said that at the current pace "there is no problem achieving that goal" and it may even be reached earlier.

Fang remains cautious about the investment amount and technical scope of Phase‑2. He noted that the key to determining the scale of investment lies in the future product mix, the technologies to be used and the target applications, which have not yet been fully defined, so it is premature to give concrete figures.

He emphasized that once the technology and product direction for Phase‑2 are settled, the company can specify the investment amount, capacity and schedule. For now, the priority is to keep listening to customer needs and ensure that the new 12‑inch investment is built on a clear, long‑term market positioning.

items.title: 紐約市議會提AI監管案！AI模型須設「關停開關」、違規最高罰2.5萬美元
items.title_en: New York City Council Proposes AI Regulation: Models Must Have a Kill Switch, Violations Fined Up to $25,000
paras: 紐約市議會近日公布一系列人工智慧（AI）監管提案，從模型上市前的第三方驗證、人工緊急關停機制，到違規舉報、損害追責與AI安全事件通報，試圖將AI安全要求轉化為具體的監管規範。
其中一項提案要求，在紐約市推廣、銷售或部署的AI模型，必須具備「kill switch」（緊急關停開關），讓人類操作人員能夠暫時或永久停止模型運作，同時接受第三方驗證。未符合要求的相關行為，擬按次處以2.5萬美元罰款。
紐約市議會9月25日公布提案後，下一個重要節點為10月5日。市議會已安排全體委員會舉行聽證，並要求包括Meta(META-US) 執行長祖克柏（Mark Zuckerberg）、OpenAI執行長奧特曼（Sam Altman）等科技業高層出席。

10月5日舉行AI監管聽證

這波立法行動早在9月25日公布提案前便已展開。
紐約市議會議長梅寧（Julie Menin）9月16日宣布，將於10月5日召開全體委員會聽證，並致函OpenAI執行長奧特曼及Anthropic執行長阿莫迪（Dario Amodei），要求兩人出席。
該委員會由紐約市51名議員組成，通常負責涉及全市重大議題的事項，較少用於立法及監督聽證。
紐約市議會表示，推動此次聽證的背景之一，是AI模型能力快速提升所引發的安全疑慮。
議會並提及Anthropic研究人員Jacob Coxon近期離職後公開警告先進AI可能帶來嚴重後果，認為有必要檢視現有防護措施是否足夠。
截至9月25日，梅寧發出的邀請對象還包括Meta執行長祖克柏、Google(GOOGL-US) 執行長皮查伊（Sundar Pichai）及馬斯克等科技業人士。
梅寧表示，市議會期待相關企業負責人出席，必要時也保留動用傳票權的可能性。

AI須具備人工關停能力　違規每次罰2.5萬美元

在具體監管條文中，人工關停能力與第三方驗證是重要要求。提案擬禁止在紐約市推廣、要約出售、銷售或部署未符合相關要求的AI模型。
所謂「關停」不只代表永久停止模型，也包括由人類操作人員讓模型暫時停止運作；第三方驗證機構則須確認這項能力確實存在且能正常運作。
驗證範圍還包括模型表現、資料來源、偏見及安全風險等。例如，模型面對與訓練資料不同的實際使用資料時如何運作、是否對受保護群體造成不利影響，以及資料處理是否安全、合法等，都納入檢查項目。
此外，驗證機構也必須揭露自身與AI模型及其開發商之間的利益關係。
對於未完成驗證或未具備人工關停能力，卻仍進行推廣、銷售或部署的行為，提案擬按次處以2.5萬美元罰款；偽造驗證資料也擬按次處以2.5萬美元罰款。其他違反該子章規定的行為，則可能面臨最高2.5萬美元罰款。
除了處罰，提案也規劃透過舉報機制取得違規線索。符合條件的個人可向紐約市消費者及勞工保護局（DCWP）提出投訴，並提供掌握的重要證據及資訊。
若政府依據舉報展開執法並追回款項，舉報人可取得追回金額的25%；若舉報人或其律師獲得授權，依規定參與訴訟或送達違法通知，比例最高可提高至50%。
另一項提案則涉及舉報人保護，擬保障揭露特定AI公共衛生或安全風險的市政府人員，以及符合條件的市政府承包商和分包商人員。
提案也將責任延伸至AI造成的損害。若第三方濫用AI造成可預見的損害，而AI提供者未採取合理防護措施，受害者可依提案規定對提供者提起民事訴訟。
至於涉及紐約市政府合約的AI安全事件，相關承包商或機構在知悉符合定義的事件後，須於24小時內通報；紐約市網路指揮機構知悉後，也須在24小時內公開規定資訊，同時保護商業機密及網路安全等敏感內容。

紐約州同步擴大AI及資料中心監管

紐約市此次提案，也是紐約州近期一連串AI監管行動的一部分。
紐約州議會2025年6月通過RAISE Act，州長霍楚爾（Kathy Hochul）同年12月19日簽署成法。根據紐約州總檢察長辦公室今年9月說明，該法將於2027年1月1日生效，要求大型AI開發商公開安全措施，並及時通報安全事件。
監管範圍也延伸至AI資料中心。霍楚爾7月14日簽署第62號行政命令，在進行資料中心環境影響評估及制定相關標準期間，暫停處理符合條件的州環境保護部門許可申請。
行政命令涉及的問題包括資料中心電力需求、用水、水質、空氣品質、噪音，以及設施對周邊社區的影響。
此外，紐約州總檢察長詹姆斯（Letitia James）9月17日也呼籲AI業界人士提供企業潛在違法行為線索，並表示可透過其辦公室的安全舉報管道匿名、保密提供資訊。
在聯邦層級，美國政府近期也開始介入AI模型的跨境測試安排。《路透》9月24日引述Politico報導，白宮曾要求OpenAI及Anthropic在接受美方審查前，暫緩向英國測試機構提供新模型。

監管能否落地　執法能力成關鍵

紐約市過去的AI監管經驗，也顯示制定規範與實際執法之間仍存在落差。
紐約市2021年第144號地方法要求雇主及職業介紹機構，在使用適用的自動化就業決策工具時符合偏見審計、結果公開及告知等要求，DCWP自2023年7月5日起開始執法。
紐約州審計長辦公室近期公布的執行審計涵蓋2023年7月至2025年6月。報告指出，DCWP期間僅收到2宗相關投訴，且未檢查投訴受理流程是否正常運作。
在企業檢查方面，DCWP檢查32家公司後僅發現1項不合規問題；州審計人員重新檢視同一批公司，則發現至少17處潛在不合規情形。
報告指出，DCWP並未使用技術部門制定的正式檢查程序，也沒有涵蓋法律要求的全部內容。部分工作人員缺乏評估相關工具所需的技術專業，卻沒有充分尋求技術部門支援；投訴處理流程也存在缺陷，無法確保所有投訴都被轉交至負責執法的部門。
這些「潛在不合規情形」並不等同於17項已確認的違法行為，但反映出檢查程序及專業支援會影響監管機構發現問題的能力。
此次提案引入舉報獎勵及第三方驗證，可能增加違規線索及專業檢查來源，但取得線索後如何調查、如何判斷驗證結果是否可信，以及最終由誰認定違規責任，仍須由執法機構處理。
即使是AI模型的「關停開關」，實際執行也涉及操作權限、停止模型後既有任務如何處理，以及連接外部工具的權限是否同步撤銷等問題。
因此，10月5日的聽證除了關注科技業者是否出席，也將涉及AI模型提供者的責任界線，以及紐約市規範如何與州級制度銜接。
分析指出，對紐約市而言，罰款只是監管機制的一環，如何發現違規、確認責任並實際完成執法，才是新制度能否落實的另一項關鍵。
paras_en: The New York City Council recently announced a series of artificial intelligence (AI) regulatory proposals, ranging from third‑party verification before model launch, to an emergency shutdown mechanism, to violation reporting, damage liability, and AI safety incident notification, aiming to translate AI safety requirements into concrete regulatory standards.

One proposal requires that AI models promoted, sold, or deployed in New York City must have a "kill switch"—an emergency shutdown that allows human operators to temporarily or permanently halt the model—and must undergo third‑party verification. Non‑compliance would be fined $25,000 per violation.

After the council released the proposal on September 25, the next key date is October 5. The council has scheduled a full‑committee hearing and has requested that senior tech executives such as Meta (META‑US) CEO Mark Zuckerberg and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman attend.

The AI regulatory hearing on October 5
This legislative effort began before the September 25 proposal was announced.

On September 16, Council Speaker Julie Menin announced that a full‑committee hearing would be held on October 5 and sent letters to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, requesting their attendance.
The committee is composed of 51 New York City council members, typically handling major city issues and rarely used for legislative or oversight hearings.
The council said one reason for pushing this hearing is the rapid improvement in AI model capabilities, which has raised safety concerns.

The council also mentioned that Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon, who recently left the company, publicly warned that advanced AI could have serious consequences, and that existing safeguards need to be examined.
As of September 25, Menin’s invitations also included Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, Google (GOOGL‑US) CEO Sundar Pichai, and other tech industry figures such as Elon Musk.
Menin said the council expects the relevant corporate leaders to attend and, if necessary, reserves the right to issue subpoenas.

AI must have an emergency shutdown capability; each violation is fined $25,000
In the specific regulatory text, the emergency shutdown capability and third‑party verification are key requirements. The proposal would prohibit the promotion, offer, sale, or deployment of AI models that do not meet these requirements in New York City.

The "shutdown" does not only mean permanently stopping the model; it also includes temporarily stopping it by a human operator. Third‑party verification bodies must confirm that this capability exists and works properly.

Verification also covers model performance, data sources, bias, and safety risks. For example, how the model behaves when faced with real‑world data that differs from its training data, whether it adversely affects protected groups, and whether data handling is safe and lawful—all are subject to inspection.
In addition, verification bodies must disclose any conflicts of interest with the AI model and its developers.

For actions that fail verification or lack an emergency shutdown capability yet still promote, sell, or deploy the model, the proposal would fine $25,000 per violation; forging verification data would also be fined $25,000 per violation. Other violations of this sub‑section could face a maximum fine of $25,000.

Beyond penalties, the proposal also plans to use a reporting mechanism to gather violation leads. Eligible individuals can file complaints with the New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) and provide critical evidence and information.

If the government acts on a report and recovers funds, the reporter can receive 25% of the recovered amount; if the reporter or their attorney is authorized to participate in litigation or serve a notice of violation, the percentage can rise to 50%.
Another proposal concerns reporter protection, aiming to safeguard city officials who disclose specific AI public‑health or safety risks, as well as qualifying city contractors and subcontractors.

The proposal also extends liability to damages caused by AI. If a third party misuses AI to cause foreseeable harm and the AI provider fails to take reasonable protective measures, victims can file civil lawsuits against the provider under the proposal.

Regarding AI safety incidents involving city contracts, contractors or agencies must report within 24 hours upon learning of an incident that meets the definition; the city’s cyber command must also disclose relevant information within 24 hours while protecting trade secrets and other sensitive content.

New York State is simultaneously expanding AI and data‑center regulation
The New York City proposal is part of a broader series of AI regulatory actions in New York State.

In June 2025, the New York State Legislature passed the RAISE Act, which Governor Kathy Hochul signed into law on December 19 of the same year. According to the New York State Attorney General’s office in September, the law will take effect on January 1, 2027, requiring large AI developers to disclose safety measures and report incidents promptly.

Regulatory scope also extends to AI data centers. On July 14, Governor Hochul signed Executive Order 62, suspending the processing of state environmental permits that meet certain criteria while data‑center environmental impact assessments and standards are developed.
The executive order addresses issues such as data‑center power demand, water use, water quality, air quality, noise, and the impact on surrounding communities.

Additionally, New York State Attorney General Letitia James on September 17 called on AI industry players to provide leads on potential violations and said that her office’s safety reporting channel allows anonymous, confidential submissions.

At the federal level, the U.S. government has recently begun to intervene in cross‑border testing of AI models. Reuters on September 24 cited Politico, reporting that the White House had asked OpenAI and Anthropic to pause providing new models to a UK testing agency until U.S. review was completed.

Will regulation take hold? Enforcement capability is key
New York City’s past AI regulatory experience also shows a gap between rule‑making and actual enforcement.

In 2021, New York City’s Local Law 144 required employers and staffing agencies to comply with bias audits, result disclosure, and notice requirements when using automated employment‑decision tools. The DCWP began enforcement on July 5, 2023.

The New York State Office of the Auditor General recently released an audit covering July 2023 to June 2025. The report noted that the DCWP received only two related complaints during that period and did not examine whether the complaint‑handling process was functioning properly.
In corporate inspections, the DCWP examined 32 companies and found only one non‑compliance issue; state auditors reviewing the same batch found at least 17 potential non‑compliance situations.

The report said the DCWP did not use the formal inspection procedures developed by the technical department, nor did it cover all legal requirements. Some staff lacked the technical expertise needed to assess the tools and did not seek adequate technical support; complaint‑handling processes also had flaws that prevented all complaints from being forwarded to the enforcement arm.

These potential non‑compliance situations are not the same as 17 confirmed violations, but they reflect how inspection procedures and professional support affect an agency’s ability to detect problems.

The proposal introduces reward for reporting and third‑party verification, which may increase violation leads and professional inspection sources, but how to investigate, how to judge the credibility of verification results, and who ultimately determines liability still need to be handled by enforcement agencies.
Even an AI model’s "kill switch" involves operational authority, how existing tasks are handled after shutdown, and whether external tool connections are simultaneously revoked.

Therefore, the October 5 hearing will not only focus on whether tech companies attend but also on the boundaries of AI model provider liability and how New York City’s regulations align with state‑level systems.

Analysis indicates that for New York City, fines are only one part of the regulatory mechanism; discovering violations, assigning responsibility, and actually enforcing the rules are the other key factors that determine whether the new system will be implemented.

items.title: 日元逼近160大關！日本再干預預期升溫、美元強勢成阻力
items.title_en: Yen Nearing the 160 Mark! Expectations of Further Japanese Intervention Rise as a Strong Dollar Becomes a Barrier
paras: 日元貶值壓力持續升高。即使美元兌日元匯率已突破日本先前進行匯率檢查時的水準，日元仍未止跌，9月24日一度升破159日元，隨著具有心理意義的160日元關口再次逼近，市場開始出現日本當局可能再次干預匯市的預期。
根據《日經》報導，外匯市場近日出現美元全面走強的情況，週四（24日）美元兌日元一度突破159日元。截至週六（26日），漲勢稍微回落，美元兌日元至157.30日元。
市場預期美國聯準會（Fed）最快可能在10月再次升息，加上美國長期利率走高，進一步推升美元買盤。
美東時間24日上午11時30分左右，美元兌日元約3週來首次升至159日元區間，此前一次觸及該水準是在9月2日。
日本央行在日本大型連假前曾向市場參與者詢問匯率水準，也就是所謂的「匯率檢查」，但即使匯率已突破當時約158日元前半的水準，日元貶值、美元升值的趨勢仍未扭轉。
Bannockburn Capital Markets策略師Mark Chandler表示，美國利率上升正推動美元走強。美國10年期國債殖利率24日一度升至約5.22%，創2007年6月以來最高水準。
在美國經濟數據表現穩健，以及油價上漲引發通膨可能持續更長時間的疑慮下，市場對聯準會10月再次升息的預期升溫。
根據FedWatch依美國利率期貨走勢計算的市場政策利率預期，截至美東時間24日下午，市場預估10月升息機率已升至約70%。
美元兌其他主要貨幣同樣走強。衡量美元相對主要貨幣強弱的美元指數升破101點，創7月底以來新高；歐元兌美元則一度跌至約1.1360美元，為7月下旬以來約2個月低點。
隨著美元兌日元再次逼近160日元，英國金融經紀商Trade Nation分析師David Morrison表示，7月底美日聯合干預對推升日元匯率所帶來的效果，已有相當一部分逐漸消退。他認為，不論美國是否參與，日元都再次接近可能迫使當局出手干預的水準。
不過，也有觀點認為，若由日本政府與日本央行單獨干預匯市，效果可能有限。主要原因在於，目前並非只有日元遭到投機資金集中拋售，而是美元走強本身具有較強的基本面支撐，其中包括市場對聯準會升息的預期。
三井住友日興證券資深利率及外匯策略師丸山凜途指出，若沒有美國參與聯合干預，或市場對聯準會升息的預期未明顯降溫，僅靠日本自身干預，恐難改變市場中期匯率判斷，使匯率轉向日元升值方向。
paras_en: The yen's depreciation pressure continues to rise. Even though the USD/JPY rate has broken the level examined by Japanese authorities earlier, the yen has not stopped falling, briefly climbing above ¥159 on September 24, and as the psychologically significant ¥160 threshold draws near again, the market is expecting possible renewed intervention by Japanese officials.

According to the Nikkei, the foreign‑exchange market has recently seen a broad strengthening of the dollar, with the USD/JPY briefly breaking ¥159 on Thursday (the 24th). By Saturday (the 26th) the rally had eased slightly, with the dollar at ¥157.30.
The market anticipates that the U.S. Federal Reserve could raise rates again as early as October, and rising long‑term U.S. yields are further boosting dollar buying pressure.
Around 11:30 a.m. Eastern Time on the 24th, the dollar rose to the ¥159 area for the first time in about three weeks, the previous touch of that level having been on September 2.

Before Japan’s major holiday, the Bank of Japan conducted a “rate check” by polling market participants, but even after the exchange rate passed the mid‑¥158 level at that time, the yen’s decline and the dollar’s rise have not reversed.

Bannockburn Capital Markets strategist Mark Chandler said rising U.S. rates are driving a stronger dollar. The U.S. 10‑year Treasury yield briefly hit about 5.22% on the 24th, the highest since June 2007.
With solid U.S. economic data and oil‑price‑driven inflation concerns lingering, expectations that the Fed will raise rates again in October have heated up.
Based on FedWatch’s calculation from U.S. rate‑futures, the market’s probability of an October hike rose to roughly 70% by the afternoon of the 24th Eastern Time.

The dollar is also strengthening against other major currencies. The dollar index, which measures the greenback’s strength versus a basket of peers, broke the 101‑point mark, a high not seen since late July; the euro slipped to about $1.1360, its lowest in roughly two months since late July.

As the dollar again approaches ¥160, Trade Nation analyst David Morrison said the impact of the late‑July US‑Japan joint intervention on lifting the yen has largely faded. He believes that, regardless of U.S. participation, the yen is once more near a level that could force authorities to step in.

However, some view that a solo intervention by the Japanese government and the Bank of Japan would have limited effect. The main reason is that it is not only the yen that is being sold by speculators; the dollar’s strength is underpinned by solid fundamentals, including market expectations of further Fed hikes.

Mitsui Sumitomo Nomura senior rates and FX strategist Rintaro Maruyama warned that without U.S. participation in a joint intervention, or without a clear cooling of Fed‑rate expectations, Japan acting alone is unlikely to shift medium‑term market sentiment toward yen appreciation.

items.title: 美元「死亡交叉」逼近 川普可能樂見其成？
items.title_en: Dollar "Death Cross" Nearing; Trump May Welcome It?
paras: 《MarketWatch》報導，目前確實有一些技術面因素，讓人相信美國財政部長貝森特(Scott Bessent)向金融市場宣告「現在我是莊家了」可能有其道理。
不僅美元的上行動能似乎已轉向日元，美元則失去優勢。同時，一個令人警戒、被稱為「死亡交叉」的技術型態正在形成，預計下周初就會確認。這意味著美元兌日元先前快速上升的趨勢可能已經反轉，而這波漲勢不僅威脅日本經濟，也不受川普政府歡迎。
死亡交叉未必是精準的市場進出訊號，但有助於強化「新趨勢可能已經形成」的觀點。Oppenheimer & Co.技術分析主管Ari Wald表示，「我們喜歡說，每一次重大的下跌走勢都始於死亡交叉，但並非每一次死亡交叉都會導致大幅下跌。」
美元兌日元周五午盤下跌1%，朝近3周來最大單日跌幅邁進。貝森特則在X平台發文，談及川普支持「強勢日元的理想性」，這也是日本銀行一直推動的方向。這波拋售出現在技術線型的關鍵時刻，進一步證明持續17個月的上升趨勢可能已經遭突破。隨著日元兌美元升值，美元兌日元匯率便會下跌。
當政府告訴投資人不要再買進某項資產時，市場有時反而會產生一種近乎反抗的興趣，選擇反其道而行，因為這可能讓人認為，當局之所以出手，是相信漲勢仍會持續，除非政府直接進場干預市場。
歷史上也有許多政府干預最終未能阻止市場走勢的案例，甚至出現極為戲劇性的結果，例如1992年英鎊崩盤、1990年代末的亞洲金融危機，以及貝森特近期試圖壓低長天期美國公債殖利率升勢的行動。
因此，當美國財政部與日本銀行在7月底合作，試圖阻止美元兌日元匯率持續攀升時，許多人認為，雖然匯率可能先行下跌，但推動匯率升至當前水準的基本面因素仍會重新發揮作用，價格很快就會恢復原本的上升軌道。
但在短暫走強後，美元兌日元匯率於9月3日跌破一條追蹤2025年4月低點以來漲勢的趨勢線。買方再度進場，推動匯率回升並測試該趨勢線，以確認這是否真的代表突破。周五的拋售則確認了這項突破。
而這波拋售發生在美元兌日元試圖重新站回200日移動均線之後。許多技術分析人士將200日移動均線視為區分長期上升趨勢與下降趨勢的重要界線。
Wald寫道，「今天在200日移動均線遭遇失敗，使該貨幣對面臨測試152支撐位的風險，該位置接近2026年的低點。」
接下來就是死亡交叉。
當50日移動均線向下穿越200日移動均線時，就會形成死亡交叉。這通常被視為短期跌勢進一步轉變為長期下降趨勢的訊號。
根據目前美元兌日元50日與200日移動均線的走勢，兩條均線預計將在下周結束前交叉。這將是該貨幣對自2025年3月25日以來首次出現死亡交叉。
上一次出現死亡交叉後，價格又下跌6%，約一個月後才觸底。
不過，再前一次死亡交叉出現在2024年9月9日，價格僅再下跌1.8%，一周後便觸底。
儘管如此，Oppenheimer的Wald認為，在目前的技術面結構下，死亡交叉「與動能全面減弱的情況一致」，並且「進一步強化了趨勢反轉的可能性」。
paras_en: MarketWatch reports that there are indeed some technical factors that make it plausible that U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s declaration to the markets “I am now the house” could have some merit.

Not only has the dollar's upward momentum apparently shifted to the yen, leaving the dollar at a disadvantage, but a warning‑sign technical pattern known as a “death cross” is forming and is expected to be confirmed early next week. This suggests that the dollar‑yen’s recent rapid rise may have already reversed, a rally that threatens the Japanese economy and is not welcomed by the Trump administration.

A death cross is not necessarily a precise market entry or exit signal, but it helps reinforce the view that a “new trend may have formed.” Ari Wald, head of technical analysis at Oppenheimer & Co., said, “We like to say that every major downtrend starts with a death cross, but not every death cross leads to a big drop.”

The dollar fell 1% against the yen at the Friday midday session, moving toward its biggest single‑day decline in nearly three weeks. Bessent posted on X, noting Trump’s support for a “strong yen,” which aligns with the Bank of Japan’s long‑standing policy. The sell‑off came at a critical technical juncture, further proving that the 17‑month uptrend may have been broken. As the yen appreciates versus the dollar, the USD/JPY rate falls.

When a government tells investors not to buy a certain asset, the market sometimes reacts with a near‑rebellious interest, choosing to go the opposite way because it may be interpreted that authorities intervene only because they still believe the rally will continue, unless they step in directly.

History is full of cases where government intervention failed to stop market moves, sometimes with dramatic outcomes, such as the 1992 British pound crash, the late‑1990s Asian financial crisis, and Bessent’s recent attempts to curb the rise in long‑term U.S. Treasury yields.

Thus, when the U.S. Treasury and the Bank of Japan cooperated at the end of July to try to halt the USD/JPY rise, many believed that although the rate might dip first, the fundamental drivers that pushed it to current levels would soon reassert themselves and the price would quickly resume its upward path.

After a brief rally, the USD/JPY rate broke below a trend line that has been tracking the rise since the low of April 2025 on September 3. Buyers re‑entered, pushing the rate back up to test that line to confirm whether it truly represented a breakout. Friday’s sell‑off confirmed the breakout.

The sell‑off occurred after the dollar‑yen tried to retake the 200‑day moving average. Many technical analysts view the 200‑day moving average as a key boundary separating long‑term uptrends from downtrends.
Wald wrote, “Today the 200‑day moving average failed, exposing the pair to a test of the 152 support level, which is near the 2026 low.”
Next comes the death cross.
When the 50‑day moving average crosses below the 200‑day moving average, a death cross forms. This is usually seen as a signal that a short‑term decline is turning into a longer‑term downtrend.

Based on the current paths of the 50‑day and 200‑day moving averages for USD/JPY, the two lines are expected to cross before the end of next week, marking the first death cross for the pair since March 25, 2025.
The previous death cross was followed by a 6% price drop, with the bottom reached about a month later.
The earlier death cross on September 9, 2024, saw only a 1.8% decline, with the bottom hit a week later.

Nevertheless, Wald of Oppenheimer believes that, given the current technical structure, the death cross “aligns with a comprehensive weakening of momentum” and “further strengthens the possibility of a trend reversal.”

items.title: 高盛上調日元目標價！12個月看升至150   日銀升息、資金回流成關鍵
items.title_en: Goldman Sachs Raises Yen Target! 12‑Month Outlook to 150 as BOJ Rate Hikes and Capital Return Become Key
paras: 日元前景出現明顯轉折，基於日本政策轉向加速，以及資金回流日本資產的可能性升高，高盛集團（Goldman Sachs）大幅調高日元匯率預測，12個月目標價由每美元兌165日元上調至150日元。
高盛策略師Karen Reichgott Fishman在最新報告中，也同步調高日元3個月與6個月目標價，分別調整至158與155。
她指出，日本央行加快升息，以及日本國內資本回流的可能性增加，是此次大幅修正日元預測的主要原因。
受相關因素帶動，日元週五一度升至每美元158.28日元。日本財務大臣片山皋月（Satsuki Katayama）此前透露，美國總統川普與日本首相高市早苗會面時，曾對日元疲軟表達關切，也為日元提供支撐。
Fishman表示，日本央行加快升息步調可能帶來雙重影響，一方面有助於抑制擴張性財政政策帶來的通膨壓力，另一方面也能減輕日元貶值壓力。
資金流動方面，她指出，日本國內資產配置資金回流的趨勢目前仍屬推測，但相關可能性正在升高，進而使美元兌日元匯率出現「下行不對稱性」（downside asymmetry），也提高日元作為投資組合避險工具的吸引力。
Fishman表示，上述發展提高做多日元的吸引力，尤其是在因應經濟衰退風險方面。
高盛並非唯一調整日元看法的主要金融機構。美國銀行此前也將年底日元預測上調至149，方向與高盛一致。
不過，高盛在短期操作策略上仍保持謹慎。Fishman表示，目前高盛較傾向放空歐元兌日元（EUR/JPY），而非直接做多美元兌日元，反映該行對近期美元走勢仍存在一定不確定性。
分析指出，高盛雖看好日元中長期走勢，但對短線行情仍維持審慎態度，反映其操作策略是看多大方向、同時留意近期市場波動。換言之，日元升值趨勢若延續，投資人仍須提防短期匯率震盪。
隨著日元已自近期低點明顯反彈，若日本政策轉向及外交相關利多持續發酵，日元後續走勢可望獲得進一步支撐。對將日元作為投資組合避險工具的全球投資人而言，高盛此次調整預期也提供了值得留意的市場訊號。
paras_en: The yen’s outlook shows a clear turning point; driven by Japan’s policy shift accelerating and the growing likelihood of capital returning to Japanese assets, Goldman Sachs has sharply lifted its yen forecast, raising the 12‑month target from ¥165 per dollar to ¥150.
Goldman strategist Karen Reichgott Fishman also raised the three‑month and six‑month yen targets in the latest report, moving them to ¥158 and ¥155 respectively.
She noted that the Bank of Japan’s faster rate‑hiking pace and the increased chance of domestic capital flowing back to Japan are the main reasons for the substantial revision of the yen outlook.

Fueled by these factors, the yen rose on Friday to as high as ¥158.28 per dollar. Japan’s Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama earlier said that during a meeting between President Trump and Prime Minister Kishida, concerns were voiced about the yen’s weakness, which also provided support for the currency.

Fishman said the BOJ’s accelerated tightening could have a dual effect: it helps curb inflation pressure from expansionary fiscal policy on one hand, and eases the downward pressure on the yen on the other.

Regarding capital flows, she noted that the trend of domestic asset‑allocation funds returning to Japan is still speculative, but the probability is rising, creating a “downside asymmetry” in the USD/JPY rate and enhancing the yen’s appeal as a portfolio‑hedge asset.
Fishman added that these developments increase the attractiveness of going long the yen, especially as a hedge against recession risks.
Goldman is not the only major institution adjusting its yen view. Bank of America previously lifted its year‑end yen forecast to ¥149, aligning with Goldman’s direction.

However, Goldman remains cautious on short‑term trades. Fishman said the firm currently prefers shorting EUR/JPY rather than directly going long USD/JPY, reflecting lingering uncertainty about the near‑term dollar trajectory.

Analysts point out that while Goldman is bullish on the yen’s medium‑to‑long‑term path, it stays prudent on short‑term moves, indicating a strategy of favoring the broader uptrend while monitoring near‑term volatility. In other words, if the yen’s appreciation continues, investors still need to watch for short‑term exchange‑rate swings.

As the yen has already rebounded markedly from recent lows, continued policy shifts and diplomatic tailwinds could provide further support. For global investors using the yen as a portfolio hedge, Goldman’s revised outlook offers a noteworthy market signal.

items.title: 〈紐約匯市〉美元漲勢暫歇本周仍漲近1% 日元因川普關切大漲
items.title_en: <New York Forex Market> Dollar Gains Pause, Still Up Nearly 1% This Week; Yen Surges Amid Trump Concerns
paras: 美元周五(25日)下跌，升至近2個月高點後暫時喘息，日元則成外匯市場焦點，終止連續5個交易日的跌勢，創下近3周來兌美元最佳單日表現。日元反彈源於東京罕見披露，美國總統川普近期與日本舉行雙邊峰會時，曾明確表達對日元疲弱的擔憂。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數(DXY)下跌0.3%，報100.97。周四曾觸及7月28日以來最高水準。
儘管美元周五下跌，美元指數本周仍上漲近1%。美元受到能源價格推升通膨的擔憂、美國公債殖利率持續飆升、強勁的美國經濟數據，以及市場重新評估聯準會(Fed)升息前景轉向更鷹派等因素支撐。
其中，美國公債遭到猛烈拋售，尤其是長天期債券，讓外匯市場參與者感到不安，也對華爾街形成壓力。本周稍早，美國10年期公債殖利率一度升至2007年6月以來最高，30年期公債殖利率則觸及2004年6月以來最高。
債券市場最初對聯準會上周升息反應正面，認為這顯示聯準會即使面臨放鬆貨幣政策的政治壓力，仍願意積極對抗通膨。
然而，聯準會官員升息後發表的鷹派言論，加上強勁的美國商業活動數據，使市場對10月升息1碼的預期升溫。
Questar Capital Partners投資長Richard Reyle表示，「2年期美國公債殖利率為4.9%，仍遠高於聯準會基準利率，這意味著未來可能還會有幾次升息，甚至可能多達3次。債市告訴我們，9月的升息並不是升一次就結束，也不是升息後暫停。對於想知道聯準會接下來可能如何調整利率的投資人而言，2年期公債殖利率提供了一張路線圖。」
日元大漲 歐元連跌3周
日元周五一度升至156.94日元兌1美元，最新報157.22日元。儘管日元反彈，但本周仍下跌0.2%。此前，日本銀行(BoJ)上周升息被市場認為力度不夠積極，導致日元承壓。
不過，周五市場情緒轉變，是因日本財務大臣片山皋月(Satsuki Katayama)於記者會上透露，川普在9月22日於紐約與日本首相高市早苗(Sanae Takaichi)會面時，曾對日元貶值表達擔憂。
片山透露，高市早苗告訴川普，「日元被低估是個問題」，並證實日本政府與美國財政部長貝森特(Scott Bessent)仍保持密切溝通，以因應雙方7月聯合干預市場後的過度波動。
《共同社》報導指出，日美兩國財長直接討論了日元貶值問題。此前日元近期一路走弱，兌美元一度跌向38年低點，突破161.80日元，而這波跌勢先前曾促使日美兩國在7月31日聯手進場干預，規模達350億美元。
歐元兌美元上漲0.2%，至1.1396美元，但本周下跌0.8%，跨大西洋公債殖利率差擴大，加上歐洲能源庫存持續不足，打壓歐元情緒。
英鎊兌美元上漲0.2%，至1.3248美元，但本周已下跌1.1%。稍早公布數據顯示，英國9月消費者信心較8月小幅改善，但整體指數仍為負值。
Interactive Brokers資深經濟學家José Torres表示，「英國消費者信心9月上升，連續第3個月改善，但根據GfK消費者信心指數，消費者仍持高度悲觀態度。此外，GfK也質疑，在持續通膨、包括能源成本上升等逆風下，消費者信心能否持續改善。」

paras_en: The dollar fell on Friday (the 25th) after reaching a near‑two‑month high, taking a brief breather, while the yen became the focus of the FX market, ending a five‑day losing streak and posting its best single‑day performance against the dollar in almost three weeks. The yen’s rebound was sparked by a rare disclosure in Tokyo that U.S. President Donald Trump, during a recent bilateral summit with Japan, explicitly voiced concern over the yen’s weakness.
In the New York close, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the greenback against six major currencies, slipped 0.3% to 100.97 after having touched its highest level since July 28 on Thursday.

Even though the dollar fell on Friday, the index is still up close to 1% for the week. The greenback is being supported by worries that rising energy prices could fuel inflation, a continued surge in U.S. Treasury yields, strong U.S. economic data, and a market reassessment that the Federal Reserve’s rate‑hike outlook has turned more hawkish.

U.S. Treasuries have been sold off aggressively, especially long‑dated bonds, unsettling FX market participants and putting pressure on Wall Street. Earlier this week, the yield on the 10‑year Treasury briefly rose to its highest level since June 2007, while the 30‑year yield hit a peak not seen since June 2004.

The bond market initially reacted positively to the Fed’s rate hike last week, interpreting it as a sign that the central bank remains willing to fight inflation even in the face of political pressure to ease policy.
However, hawkish comments from Fed officials after the hike, combined with robust U.S. business activity data, have warmed expectations for a one‑point rate increase in October.

Richard Reyle, Chief Investment Officer at Questar Capital Partners, said, “The two‑year Treasury yield at 4.9% is still well above the Fed’s policy rate, which suggests there could be several more hikes, possibly up to three. The bond market tells us that September’s hike was not a one‑off and won’t be the end of the tightening cycle. For investors trying to gauge the Fed’s next moves, the two‑year yield provides a roadmap.”
Yen rallies; euro falls for a third straight week

The yen spiked to 156.94 per dollar on Friday, later settling at 157.22. Despite the rebound, the currency is still down 0.2% for the week. Previously, the Bank of Japan’s rate hike last week was seen as insufficiently aggressive, keeping the yen under pressure.

The shift in market sentiment on Friday was triggered by Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama’s press briefing, in which she revealed that Trump, during his September 22 meeting in New York with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, expressed concern over the yen’s depreciation.

Katayama disclosed that Takaichi told Trump, “The yen is undervalued and that’s a problem,” and confirmed that the Japanese government remains in close contact with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to address the excessive volatility that followed the joint intervention in July.

According to Kyodo News, the Japanese and U.S. finance chiefs discussed the yen’s weakness directly. The yen had recently slid toward a 38‑year low against the dollar, breaching 161.80, a decline that prompted a joint intervention on July 31 worth $35 billion.
The euro rose 0.2% to $1.1396 but is down 0.8% for the week as the trans‑Atlantic yield spread widened and persistent European energy shortages dampened euro sentiment.

The pound gained 0.2% to $1.3248, yet it is down 1.1% for the week. Earlier data showed that UK consumer confidence in September improved slightly from August, though the overall index remains negative.

Senior economist José Torres of Interactive Brokers said, “UK consumer confidence rose in September for the third consecutive month, but according to the GfK confidence index, consumers remain highly pessimistic. Moreover, GfK questions whether confidence can keep improving amid ongoing inflation and rising energy costs.”

items.title: 川普關切日元走弱！片山皋月透露美日峰會內容 專家解讀「只是口頭干預」
items.title_en: Trump Worried About Yen Weakness! Katayama Reveals US‑Japan Summit Details, Experts Say “Just Verbal Intervention”
paras: 日本財務大臣片山皋月(Satsuki Katayama)周五(25日)透露，美國總統川普近期與日本首相高市早苗會面時，表達對日元走弱的關切，日元聞訊應聲上揚。
川普與日本首相高市早苗本周稍早在聯合國大會期間場邊會面，兩位領袖在會談中討論一系列議題，包括安全、中國關係，以及日本承諾對美投資5500億美元。
片山皋月周五在東京舉行記者會時說：「最近在美日高峰會上，川普總統對日元走弱表達關切。」而高市當時對川普說，日元被低估是有問題的。
片山表示，她將持續與美國財政部長貝森特(Scott Bessent)協調合作，對匯率等多項議題密切溝通。
日元周五在東京交易時段升至約158.33日元兌1美元，原先約報158.70日元。

日元貶至40年低點 美日曾聯手干預匯市

日本與美國7月底曾聯手干預外匯市場，以拉抬貶至40年低點的日元，這是兩國約28年來首次為日元採取的共同行動。
在那之後，美國聯準會(Fed)與日本銀行(央行，BOJ)先後升息，讓日元再次面臨壓力。
片山發表談話前，日元在日本五天連假後重新回到市場高度關注的160大關附近。上周美國聯準會(Fed)與日銀均升息後，日元持續走弱。
日銀在本月18日升息至1.25%後，總裁植田和男釋出進一步收緊政策的訊號，表示不排除10月連續升息，或在未來某個時間點採取更大幅度的升息。
然而，相較於Fed更加鷹派的談話，這些訊號顯得遜色。Fed在一致通過升息決議後公布的利率預測顯示，今年至少可能再升息一次，目前交易員押注Fed在接下來10月28日舉行的決策會議再度升息的機率達71%。

全球央行轉鷹 日銀升息難大幅縮小利差

Saxo Markets首席投資策略師Charu Chanana說：「我認為這基本上是另一種口頭干預。除非後續出現實際政策協調、匯市干預，或日銀將有更明確的升息路徑，否則我不認為這會對日元目前的基本走勢有任何實質上的改變。」
Bank J. Safra Sarasin外匯策略師Claudio Wewel表示，日元近期的反彈似乎建立在不穩固的基礎上。
他指出，雖然日銀官員釋出加快升息的訊號，讓長期以來拖累日元的因素正逐步改善，但從市場反應來看，日銀的政策步調與其他G10央行相比可能依舊太慢。
穆迪分析(Moody's Analytics)經濟學家Stefan Angrick表示，包括日本亞洲鄰國在內的其他幾家央行，也已轉向更鷹派的政策立場，「如此一來，日銀升息對縮小與全球其他央行間利率差距的效果，可能不如市場今年稍早預期的顯著。」
paras_en: Japan Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Friday (the 25th) that President Trump recently expressed concern about the yen’s weakness during his meeting with Prime Minister Kishida, and the yen rose on the news.

Trump and Prime Minister Kishida met on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly earlier this week, discussing a range of issues including security, relations with China, and Japan’s pledge to invest $550 billion in the United States.

Katayama told reporters in Tokyo on Friday, “At the recent US‑Japan summit, President Trump voiced concern about the yen’s weakness.” Kishida told Trump at the time that the yen was undervalued and that was a problem.
Katayama said she will continue to coordinate with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and keep close communication on exchange‑rate issues and other matters.
The yen rose in Tokyo’s trading session on Friday to about ¥158.33 per $1, from an earlier quote of around ¥158.70.

The yen fell to a 40‑year low and the United States and Japan jointly intervened in the foreign‑exchange market at the end of July, marking the first coordinated action for the yen in roughly 28 years.
Since then, the U.S. Federal Reserve and the Bank of Japan have each raised interest rates, putting renewed pressure on the yen.

Before Katayama’s remarks, the yen had bounced back toward the psychologically important ¥160 level after Japan’s five‑day holiday, after both the Fed and the BOJ lifted rates last week, further weakening the currency.

After the BOJ raised its policy rate to 1.25% on the 18th of this month, Governor Kazuo Ueda signaled the possibility of further tightening, hinting at a consecutive hike in October or a larger‑scale increase at some point in the future.

However, those signals pale in comparison with the Fed’s more hawkish tone. The Fed’s post‑decision rate outlook suggests at least one more hike this year, and traders now assign a 71% probability to another increase at the Oct. 28 policy meeting.

Saxo Markets chief investment strategist Charu Chanana said, “I see this essentially as another verbal intervention. Unless we see actual policy coordination, market intervention, or a clearer BOJ tightening path, I don’t think it will materially change the yen’s current trajectory.”
Bank J. Safra Sarasin FX strategist Claudio Wewel said the yen’s recent rebound appears to be built on a shaky foundation.

He noted that while BOJ officials’ signals of faster tightening are gradually easing the factors that have long weighed on the yen, the market’s reaction suggests the BOJ’s pace may still be too slow relative to other G‑10 central banks.

Moody’s Analytics economist Stefan Angrick said several other central banks, including those in Japan’s Asian neighbours, have also shifted to more hawkish stances, “so the BOJ’s hikes may not narrow the interest‑rate gap with the rest of the world as dramatically as markets expected earlier this year.”

items.title: 彭博：川普政府擬推海外美元穩定幣計畫 鞏固美元全球地位
items.title_en: Bloomberg: Trump Administration Plans Overseas Dollar‑Backed Stablecoin to Cement Global Dollar Dominance
paras: 知情人士透露，川普政府正在考慮一項旨在推廣在海外使用美元計價穩定幣的計畫，以鞏固美元的全球儲備資產地位。
據《彭博》24日（周四）報導，消息人士表示，穩定幣項目是美國政府考慮通過與私營企業組建合資企業來支持的領域。
該項目可能涉及多個聯邦機關，包括財政部和國務院。另有知情人士指出，美國國際開發金融公司（DFC）也可能參與其中。
DFC通常與私營部門實體合作，以推進美國外交政策目標，該機構由阿波羅全球管理公司（Apollo Global Management）共同創始人Leon Black之子Ben Black負責監管。
穩定幣是一種通常與傳統貨幣掛鉤的數位資產；隨著金融機構採用此類資產，其受歡迎程度日益提高，且目前流通的絕大多數穩定幣都與美元掛鉤。
去年美國總統川普簽署的《GENIUS法案》，確立了針對穩定幣的聯邦監管框架，要求發行方持有美元、短期國債等儲備資產。
美國財政部部長貝森特也曾表示，穩定幣的發展有望增強美元作為全球儲備貨幣的作用。
（本文不開放合作夥伴轉載）
paras_en: Insiders say the Trump administration is weighing a plan to promote the use of dollar‑denominated stablecoins abroad, aiming to reinforce the dollar’s status as the world’s reserve asset.
According to Bloomberg on Thursday the 24th, sources said the stablecoin initiative is an area the U.S. government is considering supporting through joint ventures with private firms.

The project could involve multiple federal agencies, including the Treasury and State Departments, and another source noted that the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) may also take part.
The DFC typically partners with private‑sector entities to advance U.S. foreign‑policy goals, and the agency is overseen by Ben Black, son of Apollo Global Management co‑founder Leon Black.

A stablecoin is a digital asset usually pegged to a traditional currency; as financial institutions adopt such assets, their popularity is rising, and the vast majority of stablecoins in circulation are dollar‑pegged.
Last year President Trump signed the GENIUS Act, establishing a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins that requires issuers to hold reserves such as dollars and short‑term Treasury securities.
U.S. Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen has also said that the development of stablecoins could strengthen the dollar’s role as the global reserve currency.
(This article is not open for partner re‑publication)

items.title: 〈紐約匯市〉美元徘徊近兩個月高點 油價再漲、債市拋售加劇
items.title_en: New York FX Market: Dollar Hovering Near Two-Month High, Oil Rises, Bond Sell-Off Intensifies
paras: 美元周四(24日)連續第四個交易日上漲，徘徊在近兩個月高點附近。油價再度大漲，加劇市場對通膨的擔憂，而債券市場的拋售也沒有出現緩解跡象。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數(DXY)上漲0.2%，報101.26，創7月28日以來最高。
油價周四連續第二個交易日上漲，進一步收復周二結束的連續5個交易日跌勢。油價上漲主要因美國與伊朗外交突破希望減弱。
美國總統川普與伊朗總統Masoud Pezeshkian本周在紐約聯合國大會上發表強硬演說。
川普威脅要「摧毀」伊朗並「把他們打入地獄」，否則就達成協議。德黑蘭方面則表示，伊朗「永遠不會低頭」或「屈膝」，同時表示願意進行「對話、外交與談判」。
儘管美國代表與伊朗代表團已在聯合國大會期間進行間接會談，但美國國務卿盧比歐(Marco Rubio)周三表示，他不會將這些討論形容為「重大突破」，而更像是「延續過去曾進行的對話」。
兩國在荷姆茲海峽(Strait of Hormuz)控制權問題上仍存在分歧。《路透社》周四援引接近談判人士的消息報導，美伊談判代表在紐約討論了逐步結束戰爭的方案，包括德黑蘭重新開放荷姆茲海峽，以及華府解除經濟封鎖。消息一度幫助油價收斂漲幅，但回落很快就告終。
同時，美國債券市場的拋售周四持續，美國10年期公債殖利率上升8.9個基點至5.205%，創2007年7月以來最高。
標普全球(S&P Global)周三公布的報告顯示，美國企業活動9月連續第四個月加速，創2021年7月以來最快成長速度。服務業與製造業產出均穩健成長，推動整體活動大幅增加。
同時，標普全球表示，美國9月價格壓力進一步升溫，商品與服務的平均投入成本均大幅上升，整體通膨率創2022年10月以來最高。燃料與運輸成本上升是主要推動因素。
數據顯示，美國經濟保持韌性的同時，通膨依然頑強，進一步推升市場對聯準會(Fed)10月升息的預期。根據CME FedWatch工具，市場目前預期聯準會下個月升息1碼的機率接近69%，高於一周前的約55%。
Interactive Brokers資深經濟學家José Torres表示，「市場參與者似乎認為，聯準會主席華許(Kevin Warsh)願意多次升息，以對抗主要由能源價格推動的通膨壓力。美債市場目前預期，明年夏季結束前將再升息4次、每次25個基點，總計再升息1個百分點。」
他指出，「但從購屋者與租屋者的角度來看，房價漲勢持續降溫，關稅的溫和影響大致已經過去，薪資成本也受到控制。在整體成本壓力呈現降溫而非升溫的背景下，短期內大幅緊縮似乎並不合理。」
Torres補充，「沒錯，目前通膨確實遠高於目標，但如果主要原因是供給衝擊，那麼目前市場如此迅速重新定價貨幣政策預期就沒有太大意義，因為燃料成本下降將使通膨回到接近2%目標的水準。」
習近平訪美 人民幣成焦點
人民幣周四幾乎持平，美元兌人民幣報6.7128。
當天稍早，川普在白宮接待中國國家主席習近平，這是中國國家元首自2015年以來首次赴美進行國是訪問。
川普表示，美中兩國團隊一直在合作，「促進更加平衡的貿易關係」，他也表示自己與習近平將共同「為兩國打造更美好的未來」。
貿易議題與AI預計將是川普與習近平會談的兩大焦點。
日元走弱 歐元與英鎊小幅下跌
日元連續第五個交易日走弱，美元兌日元上漲0.3%至158.84。
交易員結束連假恢復交易後，持續關注東京當局可能進行的匯市干預。近期日本銀行(BoJ)進行「利率檢查」，市場因此更加留意日本政府的干預動向。
日本銀行上周升息並未被市場視為足夠強硬。
歐洲方面，受到美元走強影響，歐元與英鎊表現低迷。歐元兌美元小幅跌至1.1380美元，英鎊兌美元下跌0.2%至1.3217美元。

paras_en: Dollar rose for the fourth consecutive trading day on Thursday, hovering near a two‑month high. Oil surged again, heightening inflation concerns, and the bond market sell‑off shows no sign of easing.
In late New York trading, the dollar index (DXY) tracking USD against six major currencies rose 0.2% to 101.26, its highest since July 28.

Oil prices rose for the second consecutive trading day on Thursday, further recouping the five‑day decline that ended on Tuesday. The rise was mainly due to hopes that a diplomatic breakthrough between the United States and Iran would ease.
U.S. President Donald Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian delivered hard‑line speeches at the United Nations General Assembly in New York this week.

Trump threatened to “destroy” Iran and “send them to hell” unless a deal was reached. Tehran said Iran “will never bow” or “kneel,” while also expressing willingness for “dialogue, diplomacy and negotiations.”

Although U.S. and Iranian delegations held indirect talks during the UN session, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Wednesday that he would not characterize the discussions as a “major breakthrough,” describing them more as a “continuation of previous dialogue.”

The two sides still disagree over control of the Strait of Hormuz. Reuters quoted sources close to the talks on Thursday, reporting that U.S.–Iran negotiators in New York discussed a phased end‑to‑war plan that includes Tehran reopening the Strait of Hormuz and Washington lifting economic sanctions. The news briefly helped oil gains narrow, but the effect quickly faded.
At the same time, the U.S. bond market sell‑off continued on Thursday, with the 10‑year Treasury yield rising 8.9 basis points to 5.205%, the highest since July 2007.

A report from S&P Global released on Wednesday showed U.S. corporate activity accelerated for the fourth consecutive month in September, the fastest growth since July 2021. Both services and manufacturing output grew solidly, driving a large increase in overall activity.

S&P Global also noted that price pressure in the United States intensified in September, with average input costs for goods and services rising sharply and overall inflation hitting its highest level since October 2022. Higher fuel and transportation costs were the main drivers.

Data indicate that while the U.S. economy remains resilient, inflation stays stubborn, further boosting market expectations for a Fed rate hike in October. According to the CME FedWatch tool, the market now assigns about a 69% probability to a 25‑basis‑point hike next month, up from roughly 55% a week earlier.

José Torres, senior economist at Interactive Brokers, said, “Market participants seem to think Fed Chair Kevin Warsh is willing to raise rates multiple times to combat inflation that is largely driven by energy prices. The U.S. bond market currently expects four more 25‑basis‑point hikes before the end of next summer, a total of another one‑percentage‑point increase.”

He added, “But from the perspective of home‑buyers and renters, house‑price gains are cooling, tariff impacts have largely passed, and wage costs are under control. With overall cost pressure easing rather than heating up, a sharp tightening in the short term does not seem justified.”

Torres further noted, “Yes, inflation is still well above target, but if the main cause is a supply shock, the market’s rapid repricing of monetary‑policy expectations matters little, because falling fuel costs will bring inflation back toward the 2% goal.”
Xi Jinping’s visit to the United States puts the renminbi in focus
The renminbi was almost flat on Thursday, with the dollar at 6.7128 per yuan.
Earlier that day, Trump hosted Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House, marking the first state visit by a Chinese head of state to the U.S. since 2015.

Trump said the U.S. and Chinese teams have been cooperating “to promote a more balanced trade relationship,” and added that he and Xi would work together “to build a better future for both countries.”
Trade issues and AI are expected to be the two main topics of the Trump‑Xi talks.
Yen weakens, euro and pound slip modestly
The yen weakened for the fifth consecutive trading day, with the dollar up 0.3% to ¥158.84.

After traders returned from the holiday break, they kept an eye on possible intervention by Tokyo authorities. The Bank of Japan’s recent “rate check” has heightened market attention to potential government intervention.
The BoJ’s rate hike last week was not seen by the market as sufficiently aggressive.
In Europe, the euro and pound were lackluster under the pressure of a stronger dollar. The euro slipped slightly to $1.1380, and the pound fell 0.2% to $1.3217.

items.title: 瑞士央行連續五次維持利率0% 軟化干預措辭
items.title_en: Swiss National Bank Keeps Policy Rate at 0% for Fifth Consecutive Meeting, Softens Intervention Language
paras: 瑞士央行周四(24日)宣布將關鍵政策利率維持在0%不變，為連續第五次會議按兵不動，符合市場預期。相較於美國聯準會、歐洲中央銀行與日本銀行等主要貿易夥伴央行相繼啟動升息循環，瑞士央行仍選擇維持利率現狀。
決議公布後，瑞郎兌美元應聲下挫0.3%，報1.2077瑞郎兌1美元；瑞士10年期公債殖利率則持穩於0.57%附近，逼近近期高點。
受中東局勢升溫與國際油價上揚影響，瑞士8月消費者物價指數(CPI)年增率回升至0.8%，但仍處於央行0%至2%的物價穩定目標區間內。瑞士央行預測2026年平均通膨率為0.7%，2027年與2028年均為0.8%。
在匯率干預方面，瑞士央行軟化了先前「增加干預意願」的強硬措辭，轉為「必要時於外匯市場採取行動」。
針對政策走向，瑞士央行總裁施萊格爾(Martin Schlegel) 表示，中期的通膨壓力僅微幅上升，當前0%的利率環境依然適當。
施萊格爾指出，先前因伊朗局勢爆發引發避險資金湧入，央行曾強力干預以防瑞郎急升；隨著瑞郎近期走弱，央行策略已轉為按需要調整外匯市場參與。面對國際升息浪潮，他強調：「我們是為瑞士制定貨幣政策。」
瑞銀集團(UBS)經濟學家在研報中指出，自6月會議以來，瑞郎兌歐元貶值逾2%、兌美元貶值逾1%，加上油價高企，大幅提高了央行提前升息的可能性，並提醒「瑞士央行歷來有出乎市場意料的傳統」。
瑞士 HIM 商學院金融學負責人Gedeon Tumong分析，瑞士享有「避險紅利」，境外資金流入支撐瑞郎，降低輸入型通膨；加上瑞士實施嚴格的「財政債務煞車機制」，無須透過提高殖利率來吸引債券投資人，因而得以維持超低利率。
paras_en: The Swiss National Bank announced on Thursday (the 24th) that it will keep its key policy rate unchanged at 0%, marking the fifth consecutive meeting of holding steady and matching market expectations. While major trading partners such as the U.S. Federal Reserve, the European Central Bank and the Bank of Japan have begun cycles of rate hikes, the SNB continues to maintain the current rate level.

After the decision was released, the Swiss franc slipped 0.3% against the U.S. dollar, trading at 1.2077 francs per dollar, and the yield on the 10‑year Swiss government bond held steady around 0.57%, near recent highs.

Affected by the escalation of tensions in the Middle East and rising international oil prices, Switzerland’s August consumer price index (CPI) year‑over‑year rate rose to 0.8%, still within the SNB’s 0%‑2% price‑stability target range. The SNB forecasts an average inflation rate of 0.7% for 2026 and 0.8% for both 2027 and 2028.

Regarding foreign‑exchange intervention, the SNB softened its earlier hard‑line wording of “increasing willingness to intervene” to a more measured “will act in the foreign‑exchange market when necessary.”
On policy direction, SNB President Martin Schlegel said that medium‑term inflation pressures have only risen marginally and that the current 0% rate environment remains appropriate.

Schlegel noted that earlier, after the outbreak of the Iran situation triggered a surge of safe‑haven flows, the central bank intervened forcefully to prevent a sharp appreciation of the franc; with the franc now weakening, the bank’s strategy has shifted to adjusting its market participation as needed. Facing the global wave of rate hikes, he emphasized: “We are setting monetary policy for Switzerland.”

UBS economists wrote in a research note that since the June meeting, the franc has depreciated more than 2% against the euro and over 1% against the dollar. Combined with high oil prices, this significantly raises the likelihood of the SNB raising rates ahead of schedule, and they reminded that “the Swiss National Bank has a tradition of surprising the market.”

Gedeon Tumong, head of finance at the Swiss HIM Business School, analyzed that Switzerland enjoys a “safe‑haven dividend,” with foreign capital inflows supporting the franc and lowering import‑driven inflation. Coupled with Switzerland’s strict “fiscal debt brake” mechanism, there is no need to raise yields to attract bond investors, allowing the country to maintain ultra‑low rates.
